thread:
ravi: 🚨 heads-up: multiple TP/PP training jobs in prod are stuck in rendezvous, NCCL TIMEOUTs showing up across 3 node pools. noticed ~5 active jobs impacted, some show 'communicator failed' in logs.

incident-bot: Paging oncall-ml and oncall-infra · Severity: P1 · Affected services: runtime-serving, training-runner · Link: https://infra.example/incident/2620001111

oncall-ml: I'm on it. first pass: gather pod and driver state, and whether this is fabric or driver-level. can folks paste kube describe + nvidia-smi output for one of the stuck pods?

ravi: paste from job job-4422 (pod train-4422-0):
```
kubectl describe pod train-4422-0 -n prod-ml
Status: Running
Events:
  Warning  Unhealthy  2m   kubelet, node-gpu-07  Liveness probe failed: dial tcp 10.0.7.9:1147: connect: connection refused

Container logs (trainer):
...
[NCCL WARN] Process 0 : Unreachable peer 2
[W ncclNet] connection timed out after 120000ms
[ERROR] NCCL ERROR: Timeout
```

sophie: also got driver side from node-gpu-07 (snip):
```
$ sudo dmesg | tail -n 60
[ 2345.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID 1002: Ch 00000000, 0000 0000 00000000
[ 2345.123460] mlx5_core 0000:3c:00.0: mlx5_core: mlx5_ib: SRQ error: transport timed out
[ 2345.123470] kernel: mlx5 pkey violation, port 1 down
```

derek: that looks fabric-related (mlx5 / rdma). link flaps + Xid errors — could be NIC firmware or cable. however several pods across two racks show the same NCCL TIMEOUT which might indicate a rendezvous failure at the NCCL level during TP/PP barrier.

oncall-infra: tagging infra now. infra-bot: please check recent mlx5 link events and if there's scheduled maintenance or config drift.

infra-bot: No scheduled maintenance. Observed 12 mlx5 link flaps on node-gpu-07 and node-gpu-08 in the last 3m. BGP/tor show no churn. PCI errors present on node-gpu-07.

anya: quick mitigations we can try (in order):
1) cordon+drain the most flappy nodes so new rendezvous avoids them.
2) restart nvidia driver on the offending node(s) (sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo systemctl restart kubelet) — do one node at a time.
3) for affected jobs: set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL to reduce cross-host sync sensitivity, or reduce pipe parallelism (pp=1) to fall back to fewer cross-node collecives.

ravi: executing 1 and 2 now on node-gpu-07 (cordon -> drain, evict pods). switching job-4422 to a fallback job config with pp=1 and batch_size=4 to reduce memory/bandwidth.

sophie: recommended log collection commands for triage:
```
# on node
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | tail -n 200
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.node-gpu-07.txt
/usr/bin/nvidia-smi -q -d PIDS,DRIVER,ERROR >> /tmp/nvidia-smi.node-gpu-07.txt
# pod logs
kubectl logs train-4422-0 -n prod-ml --previous > /tmp/pod-train-4422-0-prev.log
```

oncall-ml: collecting those now. also bumping NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for one canary job to capture communicator state.

customer-success: 2 customers running scheduled overnight fine-tuning jobs reported failures (~10% of queued tasks failed with 'communicator timeout'). both asked for ETA.

ravi: customer impact note: approx 5 active training jobs and ~20 inference pipelines on dedicated GPU pools have intermittent failures; throughput degraded ~40% for a subset of customers. we'll prepare an incident update once we have mitigation status.

derek: infra: if link flaps continue after driver restart, recommend immediate mitigation: taint node and spin up replacement nodes from a healthy pool + live-migrate (reschedule) running jobs. do not reboot all nodes at once.

oncall-infra: doing targeted cordon/drain and spinning replacement nodes. also raising RM ticket with NIC vendor — collecting PCI/sysfs dumps.

ravi: after draining node-gpu-07, jobs resumed on replacement nodes with reduced PP and NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1; timeouts dropped. one job still showing communicator reset during warmup, we forced rollback to single-GPU shard and job completed.

sophie: actionables post-mortem:
- collect full NCCL debug logs from impacted jobs (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO)
- correlate link flaps with Xid 31 occurrences
- verify NIC firmware and mlx5 drivers across node fleet (rolling check)
- add an autoscaling policy to increase node replacement buffer when collective errors exceed threshold
- add a runtime fallback rule in the scheduler: on NCCL TIMEOUT > 3 attempts, automatically attempt reduced PP/TP or reroute to dedicated non-shared pool

oncall-ml: handing to oncall-infra for root cause — oncall-infra please continue with hardware vendor engagement and fleet firmware sweep. i'll follow up with customers and draft the initial public status. handing off at ts 2620001400.

oncall-infra: acknowledged. continuing vendor engagement and cluster remediation. next update in 30m.

customer-success: thanks, please include an ETA for customer-facing note. suggest: "We are seeing intermittent GPU fabric errors affecting multi-GPU training jobs. Mitigation in progress; try reducing pipeline parallelism or using single-GPU shards as workaround. Estimated recovery: 1–2 hours."

ravi: confirmed last impacted job completed at 2620001450 after reschedule to replacement node and pp reduction. closing active mitigation. will attach logs and timeline to the incident ticket.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Final notes: 5 jobs impacted, multiple nodes showing mlx5 link flaps and Xid 31; immediate fix was node replacement and job reschedule with reduced PP. Root cause under investigation.

anya: post-incident owner assigned: oncall-infra + oncall-ml. follow-ups: fleet firmware sweep, scheduler fallback rule, improve customer-facing runbooks for NCCL TIMEOUTs.
